name: Fatty acid
oneLine: A soap-like molecule with a water-loving head and an oily tail.
howItWorks: The head likes water and the tail avoids it. In water, many fatty acids hide their tails together. They form sheets and bubbles with no help.
deeper: Fatty acids are simpler than the lipids in our own cells. Their membranes leak more, which may have helped early cells take in food.
sizeComparison: a 50,000th the width of a hair
simplification: Real membranes hold millions of these; we show a few hundred.
